target_customer: Florida and other US businesses and business owners facing employment and commercial litigation
problem: Litigation defense for small businesses is expensive and billed hourly; the firm offers fixed fees and subscription legal services supported by technology.
business_model: Law firm with fixed fee litigation and monthly subscription services, supported by affiliated tech company Spire Technical Services (CaseGuide, Inc.)

founders.name: Jesse Unruh
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and as founder in the 2020-01-16 press release. A search snippet of his profile mentions a Middle District of Florida clerkship but that source was not opened.

competitors.name: Atrium
competitors.what: Venture-backed law firm plus legal tech company offering flat fee startup legal work
competitors.funding_then: $65M round led by Andreessen Horowitz in September 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: A law firm with case management tooling; the technology is internal workflow and marketing automation, not a hard technical product.

defensibility.rationale: Bar licensing limits who can practice, but other litigation firms can adopt fixed fees and tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Atrium later grew then was not a threat to Florida employment defense; no acquisition of Spire Law found.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand beyond the firm's own pitch of fixed fees and technology; Atrium's 2018 raise shows investor interest in tech-enabled law firms.

branding.name_origin: Founding attorney said the name Spire reflects a focus on defending Florida businesses (press release 2020-01-16).

identity.logo: Text logo reading Spire Law PLLC

rebrands.why: Founder said the new name represents a focus on defending Florida businesses

brand_strength.rationale: Conventional law firm brand after a 2020 rebrand; no press about the brand beyond the rename release.

outcome_analysis: Jet.Law joined YC in Winter 2019 as a tech-enabled litigation firm, renamed itself Spire Law in January 2020 and continues as a Florida business defense firm with about 10 people. It looks like a small, self sustaining practice rather than a venture scale company; no venture funding beyond YC is confirmed.
notes: The YC page says Spire Tech Services, not Spire Law, was the YC company. CB Insights lists $150K over two rounds (seed dated 2019-03-13) and Dealroom lists a $125K seed; two aggregators disagree and neither is primary, so no round is recorded. Stanford Tech Index and a bar record place the firm in Oviedo rather than Orlando. TRUBLOOM, a class action arm named on the firm site, was not researched. Completeness pass: the 150K YC investment (7 percent stake) is reported by the Daily Business Review in 2019-03 (seen in a search snippet, page not opened). Dealroom lists a 125K seed, which conflicts and was not summed. Latka claims no outside funding, treated as unreliable.
